title: Clades and shared traits
summary: A clade is a node plus every tip that descends from it. Read trait marks — gains and losses on branches — to find clades, and meet monophyletic, paraphyletic and polyphyletic groups.

objectives: Test whether a set of tips forms a clade
Read trait marks as gains and losses on the branches below them
Tell monophyletic, paraphyletic and polyphyletic trait groups apart

items.text: Do {set} form a clade — a node plus every tip that descends from it?
items.note_after: {set} are exactly the descendants of one node — nothing left out, nothing extra.
Their common ancestor has other descendants too — a clade must include every tip below the node.

items.text: The marks show where traits changed. Are the taxa with an amnion monophyletic, paraphyletic or polyphyletic?
items.note_after: The trait arose once, and the taxa carrying it are exactly that clade — monophyletic.

items.text: Are the taxa with limbs monophyletic, paraphyletic or polyphyletic?
items.note_after: Limbs arose once on the shared stem and one lineage inside the clade later lost them — the limbed taxa are that clade minus a lineage: paraphyletic.

items.text: Are the endothermic taxa monophyletic, paraphyletic or polyphyletic?
items.note_after: Endothermy arose twice, in the mammal line and in the bird line — separate origins make the group polyphyletic.

items.text: Tap every tip that has hair.
Which trait is shared by exactly {set} — a shared derived trait of that clade?
items.note_after: A trait marking exactly one clade is a shared derived trait — a synapomorphy — of that clade.

items.text: Is endothermy in {a} and {b} homologous — inherited from a single origin — or did it arise independently?
Select every true statement about the trait marks.

statements.text: Hair arose within a lineage that already had the amnion.
The amnion arose within a lineage that already had hair.
Limbs arose within a lineage that already had the amnion.

items.text: Do {set} form a clade — and why?

reasons: They share a node that no other tip descends from.
They are drawn next to each other — neighbouring tips always form a clade.
